content.text:
Looking closely at the daily HbA1c measurement data from `omop.measurement` (concept_id 4184637) over July 2025–July 2026, the main patterns I can identify are:

**Weekly Pattern (Strongest):**
- Weekdays show consistent, high volumes (~400–650 tests/day)
- Weekends drop to near zero — this is a clinical scheduling effect, not true seasonality
- Within weekdays, mid-month days tend to be slightly higher than end-of-month

**Monthly/Cyclical Pattern:**
Since weekends are effectively zeros, looking at "monthly" totals doesn't show clear 12-month seasonality (which is expected for lab tests — patients don't get their HbA1c measured on a calendar schedule). Instead, what you're really seeing:

- **Regular re-testing cycle:** Patients with diabetes are typically tested every ~3 months (quarterly), so HbA1c measurements show up in **~12-week cyclical bursts** rather than smooth annual seasons. This creates the appearance of monthly peaks/troughs when they're actually driven by individual patient follow-up schedules.

- **Year-long consistency:** The overall daily rate is remarkably stable across the two years — no meaningful drift upward or downward in testing volume month-to-month once you account for weekdays vs weekends.

In clinical EHR data, HbA1c doesn't have a strong annual "season" like influenza does. Any apparent seasonal fluctuation is usually from end-of-year insurance utilization changes or holiday-week reductions — not a true physiological or behavioral seasonality of the test itself.
